overview_draft:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original game art-direction world overview, one high-resolution wide landscape image, approximately 16:9.
Primary request: create an art preview of DOUGH WORLD, a tiny inhabited world INSIDE living bread dough, based on a six-zone game map. This is an aspirational concept illustration, not a rendered engine screenshot. Combine soft cream dough shapes and tiny friendly dough/yeast creatures with polished painterly game concept art: broad confident shape design, hand-painted stylized materials, selective brushwork, readable foreground/middle/background, soft sun and atmospheric depth. It must feel a cohesive living organic dough landscape, not ordinary medieval grassland, not a photo of a toy, not shiny plastic.
Composition: an elevated oblique bird's-eye overview of one CONTINUOUS landscape. Map north is upper image. At CENTER a compact safe base with one arched dough hut, a small outdoor baking workbench and an open storage rack; hand-carved warm wooden furniture, flour sacks, crates and one little handcart. Around this center a shallow pale dough teaching ring, the southern foreground containing a clear gradual walking path passing a flour deposit and blue water pocket toward the base. Preserve generous traversable space and gradual slopes; don't turn every route into cliffs.
UPPER LEFT but not at far corner: warm golden active fermentation uplands, soft inflated dough folds and translucent pale mint gas bubbles, a distinctive BUTTER WATERFALL falling from the western upland edge into a golden pool and thin shallow stream flowing toward a single torn gluten wall passage connecting to the teaching ring.
FAR NORTHWEST / top-left background: higher yeast ecology plateau with clustered rounded budding yeast forms and cream-gold canopy colonies, subtle mint bioluminescent accents, tall gluten fibers, recognizably the same dough world. No purchased mushroom style, no generic forest of red fly-agaric mushrooms.
NORTHEAST / right upper-middle: a lower collapsed mold region in muted mauve, charcoal-violet and gray sage, old DOUGH settlement ruins with a few wooden remnants, delicate mycelial filaments, a clear wooden optional shortcut bridge across a fissure PLUS an open longer path around it. A large unmistakable abyss mouth lies further north/east, with a safe approach ledge.
UNDER the northeastern surface, show the sixth area as a clearly separated partial CUTAWAY into the interior side of the dough mass: a deep organic cavern, violet ambient darkness, a central corruption-core altar and tiny active-spore lights. This is underground, not a separate exposed surface biome. Suggest one descending connection from the abyss mouth; no teleport beam.
Landscape language: pale dense dough on safe high ground, bubbly porous cut faces only at selected edges, some restrained golden gluten ribbons, tiny cream fiber grass tufts clustered at edges, water cyan only in pockets, purple corruption localized. Keep density rich around landmarks but quiet along routes. Sparse tiny dough folk provide scale; no army.
Text: only a tasteful title 'DOUGH WORLD' and six small unobtrusive editorial callouts, exactly '01 BASE', '02 SHALLOW DOUGH', '03 FERMENTATION', '04 YEAST UPLANDS', '05 MOLD LOWLANDS', '06 DEEP CORE'. Do not add resource rules, statistics, brand marks, or long paragraphs. Thin callouts belong to concept-board presentation, not in-world signs. The scene remains the majority of the image.
Avoid: castles, stone fantasy towers, normal lawns/oak forests, photoreal slime, gore, overloaded resource icons, giant obstacles across the main paths, six disconnected floating islands, UI menus, artist signatures or logos.
overview_refinement:
Use case: style-transfer, art-direction revision.
Input image 1 is the generated Dough World overview to revise, preserve its six-zone spatial organization, base position, shallow teaching ring, western butter waterfall and pool, northwest yeast plateau, northeast mold lowlands with optional wooden bridge and abyss, and separate underground cutaway. Input image 2 is the user's painterly scene reference: use ONLY its broad simple painterly shapes, graphic light/shadow grouping, hand-painted color gradients, foreground-to-background atmospheric layers. Do not copy any castle, trees, composition, logos, text, signature or recognizable assets from image 2.
Revise image 1 into a cohesive colorful STYLIZED GAME CONCEPT PAINTING that could guide an Unreal game. Keep the soft cream dough identity. Replace microphotographic pores and hyperreal crumb with larger simplified rounded dough shapes, broad sculpted folds, sparse select pores on cut edges, brush-painted surface suggestions. Use elegant warm cream lights and cool lavender shadows, soft cyan water, honey butter, subtly mint yeast and mauve/sage mold. Fewer tiny details; more readable silhouettes and richer shaped clusters. Do not make a flat vector illustration.
The base is a low rounded cream dough hut with an arched doorway, small timber workbench, flour sacks and cart. Ruins are low BROKEN DOUGH arches and stumps, not fortified stone towers or castles. Make the underground deep core mysterious and gently bioluminescent, not horror, not spiky demonic architecture. Center altar a round organic dough-and-mycelium structure. Small friendly beanlike dough inhabitants for scale.
Preserve clear connecting walking paths and broad gentle slopes. Keep the panorama's title and six correct existing labels but use a clean readable restrained concept-board style. Exact labels: DOUGH WORLD; 01 BASE; 02 SHALLOW DOUGH; 03 FERMENTATION; 04 YEAST UPLANDS; 05 MOLD LOWLANDS; 06 DEEP CORE. Preserve the cutaway as a separate underground layer and don't turn it into a surface region.
Wide landscape, polished game environment concept art, clarity rather than gritty realism.

scenes.name: 01_Base_Concept
scenes.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / derive a detailed scene from the provided world overview. Asset type: one finished original environment concept PAINTING, wide 16:9, high resolution, no panels, no UI, no labels, no logos or signature.
The provided image is the established DOUGH WORLD look and world reference. Create a closer detailed scene in this SAME game world, preserving its palette, shape families, material language and consistency. This is NOT a crop or another overhead whole map. Use a cinematic three-quarter environment concept composition with clear foreground framing, playable middle ground and atmospheric background, like a hand-painted game environment illustration. Camera moderately elevated, around 25-35 degrees down; show depth and ground layout clearly. Broad simplified painterly color masses, confident rounded forms, selective brushwork, soft light and readable silhouettes. Avoid photoreal tiny pores or realistic food photography, shiny plastic, ordinary stone medieval castles, normal green meadow fantasy forest. Scale based on tiny rounded cream dough characters, only 1-3 per scene. All walking areas have broad readable ground and gentle ramps; do not introduce arbitrary obstacles or change the stage's function. The concepts are visual guidance rather than exact level dimensions.
SCENE 01: BASE BAKING COURTYARD. We stand near the base's arrival path looking toward a single rounded cream dough hut in the left-middle ground, its arched entrance open and warmly inviting. Outside on the right is an outdoor mixing and baking workbench with a wooden bowl, dough, a rolling pin, bread and flour sacks; further right, a modest open storage rack and handcart. Preserve the hut's curved dough roof as a clearly separate shape so its eventual in-game fade can be localized. Set buildings and furniture on firm dense cream dough high ground, not on a separate inaccessible floating platform. A wide foreground path leads into a generous central courtyard, all furniture at its edges. Modest golden gluten fiber tufts, crumb pebbles and small peripheral cyan moisture pockets. In the distance a hint of golden fermentation uplands and blue atmospheric silhouettes. Cozy morning sun, cream/ochre/warm timber with restrained blue-green cloth accents. No castle, no stone brick wall, no elaborate town. This should make a small practical player home and crafting yard feel recognizable and buildable.
